dataset.title: Sacramento-San Joaquin Bay-Delta Continuous (15 Minute) water quality monitoring data collected by the Continuous Environmental Monitoring Program, DWR, 2005- 2025.

abstract.para: The Continuous Environmental Monitoring Program (CEMP) plays an instrumental role in overseeing real-time water quality in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta (the Delta) and Suisun Bay. The program harnesses wireless telemetry to transmit crucial data to the California Data Exchange Center (CDEC), making high-resolution environmental data pertaining to the Delta and Suisun Bay publicly accessible. The extensive dataset captures information at 15-minute intervals from 15 monitoring stations, utilizing YSI 6600 and YSI EXO sondes to obtain standalone water quality measurements.

This extensive dataset informs the operations of the California State Water Project, ensuring it adheres to mandated water quality standards set by Water Right Decision 1641. This data compilation incorporates all information since the transition to YSI multiparameter sondes in 2005. It is important to note that the commencement dates and subsequent upgrades vary between stations, leading to slight discrepancies in the dataset's date ranges.

Since its inception in the mid-1980s, CEMP has progressively expanded its monitoring capabilities, consistently augmenting the number of monitoring locations and the array of water quality parameters assessed. Its commitment to utilizing the most advanced water quality monitoring technology reaffirms its position as an environmental monitoring leader in the Delta and Suisun Bay. Today, the program oversees 15 water quality stations that reliably capture data every 15 minutes, each day of the year, transmitting this data in real-time.
• to obtain consistent and accurate data in real-time at established monitoring stations
• to provide data necessary to achieve compliance with salinity, flow, and dissolved oxygen standards
• to perform data analyses for further understanding of estuarine ecology
• to report information to other government agencies, as well as the public, for the purpose of management
and conservation of the upper San Francisco Estuary (SFE).
• to provide continuous water quality monitoring expertise for other groups within DWR and sister agencies
for the benefit of ecological studies throughout the San Francisco- Sacramento Estuary

description.para: Data collection is ongoing and this publication will be updated at the end of each calendar year, to add the previous year's QAQC'd data.

The Continuous Environmental Monitoring Program (CEMP) monitors real-time water quality conditions throughout the Sacramento-San Joaquin River Delta and Suisun Bay. Data is transmitted to the California Data Exchange Center (CDEC) via wireless telemetry in real-time to provide information on Delta conditions. Real- time data is collected every 15 minutes, 365 days a year.

For this dataset water quality parameters were collected using YSI EXO2 multiparameter water quality sondes from Xylem (https://www.ysi.com/exo2) or YSI 6600 Series multiparameter water quality sondes (https://www.ysi.com/file%20library/documents/manuals/069300-ysi-6-series-manual-revj.pdf). Water quality parameters included in this dataset are: water temperature, specific conductivity, dissolved oxygen, fluorescence (chlorophyll), pH, and turbidity. The CEMP is the data manager and performs a daily preliminary visual inspection of the data as well as a monthly visual inspection for anomalous data or other non-representative outliers. CEMP adheres to strict calibration standard operating procedures which are performed before a sonde is deploy, CEMP does a field drift calculation, and performs a final post-deployment accuracy verification test in laboratory settings. The field drift calculation and post-deployment accuracy test are combined to calculate total drift error (environmental drift + calibration drift = total drift error). Data that is determined to be non-representative is either removed or flagged as not available. This dataset is filtered for data which have passed CEMP’s data validation procedures. Data that did not pass validation or data not collected due to equipment malfunction are reported as “NA” in this dataset. Data was downloaded from CEMP’s internal database and processed and complied in R version 4.1.0. Please use the contact for this dataset for any further QA/QC inquiries.

methodStep.instrumentation: YSI EXO2 and 6600 series multiparameter water quality sondes from Xylem

description.para: Historically, CEMP collected and reported turbidity in Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU). However, in 2021, CEMP began collecting and reporting turbidity in Formazin Nephelometric Units (FNU) to better reflect the methodology used by its turbidity sensors. NTU measurements are based on EPA method 180.1 while FNU is based on ISO 7027. Both NTU and FNU measure scattered light at 90 degrees from the incident light beam, but NTU is measured with a white light, whereas the FNU is measured with an infrared light source. The turbidity sensors manufactured by YSI that CEMP has used since 2008 follow the ISO 7027 method and thus reporting in FNU is more appropriate. According to the sensor manufacturer, NTU and FNU are comparable and no conversion of data values are required. (https://www.ysi.com/file%20library/documents/technical%20notes/t627_turbidity_units_and_calibration_solutions.pdf) Therefore, to better reflect the methodology of turbidity collection, and to be consistent with future CEMP datasets, CEMP has decided to report all turbidity measurements collected with YSI sensors in FNU.
Additional QAQC checks on the calendar year 2023 data were conducted and will continue on from 2023 to all current data.
The three additional data checks include:
- Spike testing. Set criteria to flag any point that is double the preceding and following data points (excluding turbidity).
- Water temperature and dissolved oxygen correlation. Dissolved oxygen readings depend on water temperature, if any water temperature was flagged NA, then dissolved oxygen was flagged NA as well.
- Repeated data string check. Automatically flag NA for any data that matches the exact same string as the previous measurement.

To ensure the integrity of the data, water quality monitoring stations may be relocated when necessary. These adjustments are made within reasonable parameters to accommodate changes in site accessibility, shifting environmental conditions, or updated regulatory requirements, while still maintaining the spatial consistency of the study.

methodStep.instrumentation: Prisoners Point station's location was moved to a nearby piling for improved access and to better align with existing interagency monitoring. The site was moved from 38.05630, -121.54997 to 38.05940, -121.55720 on September 3rd, 2025.
